name: Tokyo Weekend
summary: A 2-day sprint through Tokyo — Shibuya, Shinjuku, Asakusa, and Akihabara. Temples in the morning, arcades at night, yakitori in between.

stops.name: Haneda Airport (HND)
stops.note: Arriving Friday night. Take Keikyu Line to Shinagawa, transfer to JR Yamanote to Shibuya.

stops.name: Shibuya Excel Hotel Tokyu
stops.goal: Overnight stay — connected to Shibuya Station, unbeatable location
stops.note: Mark City complex, directly connected to the station. Ask for a high floor — the scramble crossing view is worth it.

alts.name: Dormy Inn Premium Shibuya Jingumae
alts.goal: Budget-friendly alternative with an onsen on the top floor

stops.name: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
stops.goal: Stand at the world's busiest pedestrian crossing — it's a Tokyo rite of passage
stops.note: Best viewed from Starbucks Tsutaya 2F (free, but busy) or Magnet 7F rooftop (¥500, less crowded). Go early — it's a mob by 10am.

stops.name: Meiji Jingu
stops.goal: Walk through massive torii gates into a forest in the middle of Tokyo — the city's most important Shinto shrine
stops.note: Free entry. Closes at sunset. Buy an omamori (charm) — they make great small gifts. The sake barrel display near the entrance is photo-worthy.

stops.name: Takeshita Street (Harajuku)
stops.goal: Crepes, vintage shops, and peak Tokyo people-watching
stops.note: The crepe stands at the entrance are the real deal. For vintage, duck into the side streets — Takeshita itself is mostly fast fashion.

alts.name: Cat Street, Harajuku
alts.goal: Quieter, cooler alternative to Takeshita — indie boutiques and better coffee
alts.note: Connects Harajuku to Shibuya. Good if Takeshita's crowds get to you.

stops.name: Omotesando
stops.goal: Walk Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — flagship architecture and design shops
stops.note: Stop at Koffee Mameya for a pour-over — it's a tiny standing-room-only coffee bar in a converted warehouse.

stops.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
stops.goal: Escape the concrete — greenhouse, French Formal Garden, and Japanese garden in one park
stops.note: Closes 5:30pm, last entry 5pm. The Japanese garden section is the highlight — find the tea house.

stops.name: Omoide Yokocho (Piss Alley)
stops.goal: Dinner in a post-war alleyway of yakitori stalls — the Tokyo that tourists hope to find
stops.note: Cash only at most stalls. Get there before 6pm for a seat — the best stalls fit 6 people and fill instantly. Try the shiitake skewers even if you think you want meat.

alts.name: Nakajima, Shinjuku
alts.goal: Michelin-starred sardine set lunch for ~¥800 — one of Tokyo's best food deals
alts.note: Lunch only. Line forms at 11am. The iwashi teishoku is what you're here for.

stops.name: Golden Gai
stops.goal: Bar hop through 200+ micro-bars in six narrow alleys — each bar seats 5-8 people max
stops.note: Many bars have cover charge (~¥500-1000). Bar Albatross is foreigner-friendly and a good starter. Don't take photos in the alleys without asking — some bar owners are strict about it.

stops.name: Sensō-ji
stops.goal: Tokyo's oldest temple — get there before the crowds for the best experience
stops.note: Nakamise-dori shops open ~10am. Before 9am you'll have the main hall nearly to yourself. Get your fortune (omikuji) — if it's bad, tie it to the rack and leave the bad luck behind.

stops.name: Sumida River Walk
stops.goal: Walk the river terrace toward Skytree — best photo angles of the tower
stops.addr: Sumida River Terrace, Taito City, Tokyo 111-0032
stops.note: Coffee at Fuglen Asakusa — Scandinavian-Japanese hybrid in a restored ryokan. The river walk is a 5-min detour from Sensō-ji.

stops.name: Lunch in Asakusa
stops.goal: Unagi (eel) or tempura in one of Tokyo's oldest neighborhoods
stops.note: Unatoto for casual unagi (counter seating, ¥2000-3000). Daikokuya for tempura (cash only, the tendon is legendary).

alts.name: Sometaro, Asakusa
alts.goal: Cook-your-own okonomiyaki in a 60-year-old restaurant — fun and interactive
alts.note: Floor seating on tatami. Great if you want a break from sushi and ramen.

stops.name: Akihabara Electric Town
stops.goal: Retro games, arcades, anime, and the sensory overload of Tokyo's tech district
stops.note: Super Potato (retro games, 5th floor) is the pilgrimage site. Yodobashi Camera for everything else. The Sega arcades are gone but Taito HEY is still going strong.

stops.name: Tonkatsu Marugo
stops.goal: Legendary tonkatsu — thick-cut, perfectly fried, worth the line
stops.note: Opens 11:30, line forms early. Only ~12 counter seats. The hire-katsu (lean fillet) and rosu-katsu (fatty loin) are both correct — get the rosu.

alts.name: Kyushu Jangara Akihabara
alts.goal: Famous tonkotsu ramen — faster than Marugo, just as satisfying
alts.note: Open all afternoon. The karashi (spicy) miso tonkotsu is what you want.

stops.name: Haneda Airport (HND)
stops.note: Arrive by 6pm. Keikyu Line from Shinagawa. The observation deck at Terminal 3 is a solid farewell — open-air views of the runway and Tokyo Bay.

routes.note: Keikyu Line to Shinagawa, transfer to JR Yamanote (counter-clockwise) to Shibuya.
Walk through Miyashita Park for a rooftop detour — good for a quick coffee at the start.
Exit Meiji Jingu via the Harajuku gate — Takeshita Street is right there.
Walk down Omotesando Ave. Stop at Koffee Mameya for pour-over.
Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line from Omotesando to Shinjuku-gyoemmae (3 stops).
Exit garden at Shinjuku gate, walk through the station area toward the west exit.
Through the east side of Shinjuku station, past Kabukicho signs. 10 min walk.
JR Yamanote to Ueno, transfer to Tokyo Metro Ginza Line to Asakusa. ~40 min.
Cross the street behind Sensō-ji to reach the river terrace. 5 min.
Tsukuba Express from Asakusa to Akihabara (2 stops).
JR Yamanote to Shinagawa, transfer to Keikyu Line to HND.

days.note: West Tokyo — Shibuya, Harajuku, Omotesando, Shinjuku. Day 1 is a greatest-hits tour of Tokyo's west side.

items.txt: Grab breakfast at the hotel or a konbini — FamilyMart onigiri + Boss coffee is the authentic Tokyo morning

opts.txt: Karaoke in Shinjuku — try a Kan Kan location for cheap all-you-can-drink

items.txt: Last Yamanote train ~12:50am — don't miss it back to Shibuya

days.note: East Tokyo — Asakusa, Akihabara, and depart. Temples in the morning, arcades in the afternoon.

opts.txt: Ramen at Kyushu Jangara Akihabara (famous tonkotsu, open all afternoon)
